name_vi: Tỷ lệ dài trên rộng của khuôn mặt
what_it_controls: Whether the face reads long or wide at any crop. It is the single parameter that survives being resized to a 40px avatar, so it does more identity work than any feature
failure_when_wrong: Drift here is what makes a virtual model look like a different person between two posts while every individual feature still matches
prompt_phrasing: face length to cheekbone width about 1.40 to 1
source: Facial index is standard craniofacial anthropometry (bizygomatic width, menton to trichion). Verify the landmark definitions before quoting the term

name_en: Jaw width relative to cheekbone width
name_vi: Chiều rộng xương hàm so với gò má
what_it_controls: The taper of the lower face. Low values read as a narrow jaw, values near 1.0 as a square one
failure_when_wrong: This is the parameter image models drift most under a beauty prompt, always toward a narrower jaw. If it is not written down it will not survive ten generations
prompt_phrasing: jaw width about three quarters of cheekbone width
source: Gonion and zygion are standard anthropometric landmarks; confirm before citing

name_vi: Độ nghiêng trục mắt
what_it_controls: The angle of the line from inner to outer eye corner. It sets whether the eye reads upturned or downturned, which is most of what people mean by expression at rest
failure_when_wrong: Left unspecified, a generator will fluctuate between frames and the same person will read alternately sharp and sleepy
prompt_phrasing: slightly upturned outer eye corners, about four degrees
source: Medial and lateral canthus are standard terms; the tilt measure is used in oculoplastic literature. Verify a source before quoting a range as typical

name_en: Eye spacing relative to face width
name_vi: Khoảng cách hai mắt so với bề rộng mặt
what_it_controls: How far apart the eyes sit. Together with the facial index it accounts for most of the resemblance a viewer registers before they can name a single feature
failure_when_wrong: The most common cause of a virtual model that is recognisable in close-up and a stranger at half-body distance
prompt_phrasing: eye spacing a little under half the face width
source: Interpupillary distance is standard optometric measurement; the ratio to bizygomatic width is the composition of two standard measures

name_vi: Phân chia ba phần khuôn mặt
what_it_controls: Where the brow line and the nose base fall down the face. Shifting weight into the lower third reads as a longer chin; into the upper third as a higher hairline
failure_when_wrong: A face specified only by features and never by its thirds is a face the model will re-proportion every render
prompt_phrasing: brow, nose base and chin dividing the face into roughly equal thirds
source: The thirds layout is standard figure and portrait drawing instruction; cite an instruction text, not a beauty-canon claim

name_en: Nose width relative to mouth width
name_vi: Bề rộng mũi so với bề rộng miệng
what_it_controls: The relationship between the two features that sit on the same vertical axis, which is what makes the centre of the face read as one structure rather than two
failure_when_wrong: Specify the nose and the mouth separately and they will each be plausible and jointly wrong
prompt_phrasing: nose width about seven tenths of mouth width
source: Alare width and cheilion-to-cheilion are standard landmarks

name_vi: Tỷ lệ môi trên và môi dưới
what_it_controls: The visible red of the upper lip against the lower. This is the parameter an overlined-lip makeup look changes, so lock it bare and let the makeup row do the styling
failure_when_wrong: Confusing this with the makeup means the model's mouth changes shape every time the campaign changes lipstick
prompt_phrasing: lower lip about one and a half times the upper
source: Vermilion is the standard term for the visible lip; verify before quoting proportions as typical

name_en: Philtrum length as share of lower third
name_vi: Chiều dài nhân trung trên phần ba dưới
what_it_controls: The distance from nose base to upper lip. Small changes here move the whole apparent age and are almost never specified, which is why they drift
failure_when_wrong: Unspecified, this is where a generator quietly ages or de-ages a locked character between campaigns
prompt_phrasing: short philtrum, under a quarter of the lower face
source: Philtrum, subnasale and labiale superius are standard landmarks

name_vi: Khoảng cách từ chân mày đến mí
what_it_controls: How much lid space is visible. This is the surface every eyeshadow look in makeup-looks.csv is painted on, so the look and the space have to be specified together
failure_when_wrong: A graphic editorial eye specified onto a shallow lid comes back either flattened or with the brow relocated
prompt_phrasing: moderate visible lid space between brow and lash line
source: Composed from two standard measures for this skill; no single standard term found for the ratio

name_en: Forehead height as share of face length
name_vi: Chiều cao trán trên chiều dài mặt
what_it_controls: Where the hairline sits, which is the parameter a fringe hides. Lock it anyway, because the fringe is styling and will change
failure_when_wrong: A character locked only in a fringed hairstyle has no defined face above the brow, and the first swept-back styling reveals a different person
prompt_phrasing: hairline at roughly a third of the face length
source: Trichion is a standard landmark

name_vi: Một nét bất đối xứng hoặc dấu riêng
unit: named location and size in mm-equivalent
input_domain: exactly one, stated with a side
what_it_controls: The thing that makes the face a person rather than an average. A mole above the left jaw, a slightly lower right brow, one crooked lower incisor
failure_when_wrong: A perfectly symmetric face is the strongest single tell of generated imagery, and it is also unownable - it is the average of the training set, so it belongs to nobody and resembles everybody
prompt_phrasing: small mole two centimetres above the left jaw line, right brow sitting marginally lower
source: This skill's own rule, from slop-tells.csv on generated-face symmetry

name_vi: Chiều cao tính theo số đầu
what_it_controls: Overall proportion without ever stating a height in centimetres, which is what makes the sheet work at any crop and in any country
failure_when_wrong: Fashion illustration convention runs to 8.5 or 9 heads and an image model has absorbed that. Unspecified, a full-body frame will drift toward illustration proportions and stop matching the half-body frames
prompt_phrasing: natural proportions, about seven and a half head heights
source: The head-unit canon is standard figure-drawing instruction (Loomis, Bridgman, Hogarth); cite an instruction text

name_vi: Bề rộng vai theo đầu
what_it_controls: Frame width at the top of the figure, which sets how the garment hangs and how much of the background the silhouette covers
failure_when_wrong: Left open, this is the axis a generator moves to make a figure read as authoritative or delicate, so the same character changes build with the mood of the prompt
prompt_phrasing: shoulders about two head widths across
source: Standard head-unit figure instruction; verify the term with a source

name_vi: Tỷ lệ vai trên eo
what_it_controls: Torso taper. With shoulder width it fully specifies the upper body outline, which is what apparel photography is actually selling
failure_when_wrong: Describing a build with an adjective instead of this ratio is how a clothing brand ends up with a model whose proportions differ between the flat-lay frame and the on-model frame
prompt_phrasing: modest taper from shoulder to waist, about 1.3 to 1
source: Composed from standard head-unit instruction

name_en: Leg length as share of stature
name_vi: Tỷ lệ chân trên tổng chiều cao
what_it_controls: Where the waist sits in the frame, which decides where a full-body composition can be cropped without cutting the figure at a joint
failure_when_wrong: Unspecified, it interacts with the head-unit count and the figure comes back elongated below the waist only - the specific distortion that reads as an AI fashion image
prompt_phrasing: legs slightly under half the total height
source: Standard figure instruction; verify

name_vi: Chiều dài cổ theo đầu
what_it_controls: The gap between jaw and shoulder line. It decides whether a chin-forward pose is available at all, and whether a high collar covers the whole neck
failure_when_wrong: A short neck plus a chin-elevation instruction produces the compressed jaw that gets read as a bad render rather than a bad pose
prompt_phrasing: neck a little over a third of a head height
source: Standard figure instruction; verify

name_vi: Dáng đứng mặc định
unit: degrees of thoracic lean and shoulder drop
what_it_controls: How the person stands when not posing. A consistent small asymmetry is what makes a series of frames read as one human being
failure_when_wrong: Perfect posture in every frame is the second-strongest generated-image tell after facial symmetry
prompt_phrasing: weight settled, right shoulder marginally lower, very slight forward lean
source: This skill's own axis; the shoulder-drop observation comes from reference-observations.csv

name_vi: Phân bố trọng lượng lên chân trụ
what_it_controls: The root of every standing pose. The leg carrying the weight is the engaged leg and the other is the free leg; moving off 50/50 is what stops a figure reading as a mannequin
failure_when_wrong: Even weight makes a standing figure inert. It is the correct choice only when the styling is doing all the work and stillness is the point
prompt_phrasing: weight on the left leg, right leg relaxed and slightly bent
source: Engaged and free leg are the standard terms in the contrapposto literature; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contrapposto

name_en: Counter-rotation between hip line and shoulder line
name_vi: Độ xoay ngược giữa trục hông và trục vai
what_it_controls: This is contrapposto stated as a number. Weight on one leg raises that hip; the shoulder on the same side drops, so the two axes tilt in opposite directions and the spine takes an S
failure_when_wrong: Zero counter-rotation with an off-centre weight is the uncanny standing pose: the hips are doing something the shoulders have not answered
prompt_phrasing: right hip raised, right shoulder dropped, about twelve degrees of opposition
source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contrapposto - hips and shoulders at opposite levels in the frontal plane, engaged leg straight, free leg slightly bent

name_vi: Độ xoay thân so với chính diện
what_it_controls: Frontal at 0, three-quarter near 30 to 45, profile at 90. Three-quarter is the default for a person because it shows two planes of the torso and narrows the silhouette at the same time
failure_when_wrong: Full frontal at 0 reads as an identity document unless the pose is deliberately inert; full profile hides the product side of the body
prompt_phrasing: torso turned about thirty degrees off camera, face returning to the lens
source: Frontal, three-quarter and profile view are standard portrait terms

name_vi: Đường chuyển động chính
unit: named curve: straight, C, S, reverse-S
what_it_controls: The single curve running from head through the weight-bearing foot that the whole pose is built on. Drawn first in figure instruction, and the reason a pose reads as one gesture and not a set of arranged limbs
failure_when_wrong: Posing limb by limb with no line of action gives a figure that is correct joint by joint and lifeless overall. This is the difference people cannot name when they say a photo looks stiff
prompt_phrasing: a single soft S running from the head down through the standing foot
source: Line of action is standard figure-drawing instruction; the S-curve is documented alongside contrapposto

name_en: Negative space between arm and torso
name_vi: Khoảng trống giữa tay và thân
what_it_controls: Whether background is visible between the upper arm and the waist. A visible gap separates the arm from the body and is what makes a waist readable at all
failure_when_wrong: Zero gap fuses arm and torso into one mass, so the figure widens and the waist disappears. It is the commonest reason a good pose photographs badly, and it is invisible to the person posing
prompt_phrasing: clear gap of background visible between the upper arm and the waist
source: Negative space and tangency are standard composition terms in figure and photographic instruction

name_vi: Kiểm tra tiếp tuyến và chồng chi
input_domain: pass required at wrist, elbow, knee, ankle, crown
what_it_controls: Whether a contour of the figure runs exactly along a background edge, and whether the frame cuts a limb at a joint. Both read as an error even when nothing is wrong with the pose
failure_when_wrong: A frame cropped at the wrist or ankle reads as amputated; a shoulder line coincident with a horizon line flattens the figure into the background
prompt_phrasing: crop between joints, not at them; keep the figure contour off the background edges
source: Tangency is a standard composition fault in photographic instruction; verify the term with a source

name_vi: Độ nghiêng đầu
what_it_controls: Lateral tilt of the head, independent of rotation. A few degrees reads as attention; past about twelve it becomes a performed cuteness that dates fast
failure_when_wrong: Tilt with no counter-rotation in the shoulders reads as a broken neck rather than a gesture
prompt_phrasing: head tilted about five degrees toward the raised shoulder
source: Standard portrait direction vocabulary

name_vi: Độ hạ nâng của cằm
what_it_controls: Pitch of the head. Slightly down defines the jaw line and shortens the nose; up exposes the underside of the jaw and the nostrils
failure_when_wrong: A dropped chin plus a low camera is the pairing that produces a double chin in an otherwise correct frame. This parameter is meaningless without the camera height beside it
prompt_phrasing: chin lowered about three degrees, jaw line held long
source: Standard portrait direction vocabulary

name_vi: Độ lệch hướng nhìn so với ống kính
what_it_controls: Whether the subject looks into the lens. Zero is address, and it is the choice that makes a frame feel spoken to the viewer; off-axis needs a reason in frame or it reads as avoidance
failure_when_wrong: Off-axis gaze with nothing for the subject to be looking at is the single most common unforced error in small-brand photography
prompt_phrasing: looking directly into the lens
source: Standard portrait direction; the in-frame-reason rule is recorded in reference-observations.csv

name_en: Working hand height relative to the eyeline
name_vi: Độ cao của tay so với đường mắt
unit: head units above or below eyeline
what_it_controls: Where the occupied hand sits. At the eyeline it becomes a second focal point at the same height as the face; above the crown it outranks the face entirely
failure_when_wrong: Empty hands hanging at the hip is what makes a person look like they are waiting rather than working. Every frame in the four-post salon set has one forearm raised into frame holding something from the set
prompt_phrasing: one forearm raised into frame at eye height, holding the product
source: reference-observations.csv, aespa-kissntell-one-set-four-posts and the height-beats-size rule in reference-reading.md

name_vi: Cách tạo hình bàn tay
what_it_controls: What the fingers are doing. Fingers relaxed into a slight curl, or in contact with a surface, or closed around an object - never straight and spread
failure_when_wrong: A flat splayed hand shows every finger in full length, which is the pose generators render worst and the one that most often comes back with the wrong finger count. Giving the hand an object to close around removes the failure instead of hoping past it
prompt_phrasing: fingers relaxed and slightly curled, closed around the object
source: This skill's own rule; the object-in-hand fix is observed in reference-observations.csv

name_vi: Tiêu cự quy đổi 35mm
what_it_controls: Perspective on the face, via the subject distance it forces. It is not the lens that distorts a face, it is standing close - and a short lens is what makes you stand close to fill the frame
failure_when_wrong: A prompt asking for a wide lens and a tight head-and-shoulders crop is asking for an enlarged nose and receding ears. The two instructions are in conflict and the model will satisfy the crop
prompt_phrasing: 85mm equivalent, head and shoulders
source: Perspective distortion is a function of subject distance, not focal length as such; find and cite the published work before stating a preferred focal length

name_vi: Khoảng cách từ máy đến người
what_it_controls: The actual cause of facial perspective. State it alongside the focal length so the two cannot contradict each other
failure_when_wrong: Omitted, this is the hidden variable behind every complaint that a portrait looks wrong for reasons the person cannot name
prompt_phrasing: camera about two and a half metres from the subject
source: Same as focal-length; verify against the published perspective-distortion work

name_en: Camera height relative to the subject eyeline
name_vi: Độ cao máy so với đường mắt
what_it_controls: Level with the eyes reads as address between equals. Above reads as looking down on the subject, below as looking up at them. This is the fact most people never record and the one that most reliably reproduces a reference
failure_when_wrong: It must be set together with chin elevation. Low camera plus dropped chin is the jaw-line failure; high camera plus raised chin flattens the face
prompt_phrasing: camera level with the eyes
source: reference-reading.md question 4; standard camera-direction vocabulary
